about: Which semantic lanes belong in one subagent, for a native (Claude subagent) review. The lanes are leaves of a binary tree whose internal nodes join lanes that read the same bytes, so a subagent opens each file once; `compose-native-pairs.py --agents N` cuts the tree into exactly N total subagents by repeatedly splitting the group with the most lanes into its two children (ties go to the left one). Lanes in `alone` always run by themselves, each in its own subagent, and count toward N. Lanes with no prompt are pruned out first, so a tier's smaller lane set is grouped by the same themes. A lane whose report is another lane's trigger (1 and 31) never share a group until N is large enough to separate everything else. Fewer, larger groups trade independence and report depth for fewer launches; each lane still gets its own report.
